answer: A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 60 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. The jetty detector writes to oasis, and onyx makes public every merge. Submissions that land within 189 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 25 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
